reason: The publisher correction is right and I confirmed it at the best available authority: the bibliography on adriennerich.net, reproduced from Jane Roberta Cooper’s bibliography in Reading Adrienne Rich (University of Michigan Press, 1984), lists Snapshots of a Daughter-in-Law: Poems 1954-1962 (Harper, 1963; W.W. Norton, 1967). So Harper and Row 1963 is the first edition and Norton 1967 is the reissue, exactly as the verifier says, and the proposal’s Norton first edition was wrong. The poem is dated 1962 and sits inside the book’s stated span. Mechanical checks clear: shipped.js gives no exact hit, no near hit, Rich at zero for the year, not banned; 1963 is in scope; the tag Poetry is the form of the work; the source line is 119 characters, leads with the name, carries hyphens only and no dash, no straight quote; the quotation ends in a full stop. I attacked the lineation hard, because that is what the card asserts with its two slashes, and it survives but not as cleanly as the verifier claims. Reputable reproductions disagree. BillMoyers.com prints the close as two lines, The door itself makes no promises. / It is only a door., and it keeps every earlier stanza correctly in threes, so it is not simply reflowing; AllPoetry prints the same two line close, and josieholford.com copies the Moyers text. Against that, exceptindreams and best-poems.net print three lines, and the decisive witness I found is David Biespiel in The Rumpus, 11 October 2016, who quotes the close inline with his own slashes as The door itself / makes no promises. / It is only a door, a deliberate marking of line breaks by a poet writing about the poem, in an essay whose own block quotation had lost the stanza breaks. Three lines also completes the poem as seven clean tercets. I therefore let it stand, but the verifier’s word confirmed overstates what two aggregator sites can carry: no scan or facsimile of the 1963 Harper and Row leaf was reached, and the note should say that the three line close rests on secondary witnesses and that some reputable reproductions run the last two lines as one.
